#4057. Poll: What Review Score Would You Give The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake?

It's here. It's finally here, and we'd wager you've spent a good chunk of the past 48+ hours playing it. Or perhaps you're savouring the moment, waiting for the perfect time to settle down with the most critically acclaimed game of the year (so far).

Either way, Ocarina is out on Switch 2, and millions of you have had the opportunity to dive into this beautifully reimagined version of a Hyrule that's near and dear to so many of us.

As mentioned, it's gone down very well with critics and currently sits with a whopping great Metascore of 96 after 85 reviews. Our own Ollie Reynolds called it "a remarkable remake, and a must-buy for Switch 2" in his 9/10 review:

"Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is a stellar reimagining of the original, one that completely revamps the experience with stunning visuals, modernised gameplay, and vastly improved audio. Despite some minor blemishes, this is comfortably the most visually stunning work Nintendo has ever put out, and it’s unquestionably the best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time."

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

Now that the game has been out a couple of days, though, it's time to start canvassing public opinion: What score would you give this particular OoT?

No worries if you haven't played it yet or don't feel comfortable scoring it right now - you can return and rate the game at any time by revisiting this page or heading to our game page. As quickly as Ocarina veterans may have bolted through it, this is still a sizeable adventure, especially if you never played the original!

If you have played enough to form an opinion, though, let us know below how many numbers out of 10 you'd award the remake. (And remember, you're free to change your mind and adjust your rating at any time.)

Please note voting will score the game in your games collection

The tightrope balance of keeping the feeling (cinematic and scope) while still amazing (as in to make someone amazed) the player is being well kept. There are areas of the game that make me viscerally uncomfortable (or elated) even though I know they are there.

This game is what nostalgia truly means. Not some ruined or derided longing for better days, but the ability to have core memories and associations strummed by an evocative experience. This game does this as I find myself giggling or shuddering or laughing or trying not to tear up. At the same time it is FUN. I miss pure adventure games in a world of open world procedurals (BOTW and TOTK managed to avoid this feeling), get gud death runs, and epic rpgs where I need a spreadsheet to keep track of choices made so I get the ending I want. I just want to wander, and perhaps find some new connection.

I can smile and be curious about the varied NPCs and make up little thought about their inner lives without having the game having to keep a realistic schedule. Also, oddly enough and I hate to say this, no romance. Just two kids chosen by destiny to stop a big bad in a world of magic. (I know there are shippers in every fandom. I don’t see it, so leave me alone). The presentation is beautiful, the gameplay and control design smooth and with no technical issues It feels like the storytelling quirks of all the Zelda games were neatly layered on to make the characters feel more vibrant, while leading with OoT’s narrative style.

If BOTW was LoZ (first game) fully realized, then this S2 OoT is OoT fully realized. It feels like a memory, it feels like a reunion, it feels like a link to the future. It is the best way to play OoT. What a time to be a Zelda fan.

First they put a Zora holding a bottle in around the fish area, then they have the signpost in Zora's fountain literally saying "give an offering to Jabu," then a pool of water directly in front of Jabu, perfect for a fish. If you have played the game before, I'd score it an 8, since the handhold-y bits wouldn't bother you (you know exactly what to do anyway). I completed the game fully about half an hour ago. I’ve been visiting this site for years but have never made an account, but after playing this felt compelled to.

I’m going straight in to say I gave this game a 10/10 - I can’t quite believe what I’ve just experienced. I have so many emotions, thoughts, feelings coursing through my body and mind, I’m not quite sure I can say anything coherent.

This was my first Zelda game which I played in 2000 when I was 11. It captivated me then and never let go; I have revisited this game at least once per year ever since, including the incredible 3DS version. I was one of those who longed for this remake and to say it delivered and exceeded expectations is an understatement.

When the trailers were first revealed, I wasn’t sure about the character models and the English voice acting (American accents, ugh, I agree with the other poster who said that they just don’t fit this epic/heroic/mythological type stories, whether movies or games). Thankfully, the remake allows you to play with the Japanese voice actors which I changed the game to as soon as I was able (hearing Navi with that preppy American speak I so detest was an instant nope). The voice acting was sublime in Japanese and really drew me into the world.

And what a world! The game is beyond gorgeous, and I found myself smiling so many times throughout; I also gasped, laughed, chuckled and had a little cry at times (I had a big cry during the end!). The original Ocarina of Time was a straight 10 for me, and this is the same game, just remade in 2026. There has been much criticism that it plays too safe, but I wanted Ocarina and that’s what I got. There were just enough changes that some small parts were new and unfamiliar which I found very enjoyable, and I enjoy all the changes. I loved being able to walk into Lake Hylia and Lon Lon Ranch without loading screens, and having night versions of some of the tracks was a cherry on top.

The soundtrack! It is magnificent; I have no other word to describe it. OOT is one of the greatest soundtracks ever created in gaming, and this versions arrangements elevate and enhance what was already stellar.

One of the strongest aspects of the original Ocarina was the atmosphere, and I was overjoyed to discover that this version perfectly portrayed the atmosphere, again in some places enhancing it. It’s strange how often I truly felt that this was the game as I’d always played it, despite knowing that wasn’t true. There will always be room in my life to revisit the N64 and 3DS versions from time to time, but henceforth this is the definitive version (I am slightly baffled that NL reviewer said it isn’t the definitive version, perhaps due to the lack of Master Quest, but as someone who has never played Master Quest beyond Dodongo’s Cavern, it was no loss to me).

I think the reason why Ocarina of Time captivated and stayed with me since the day I started playing it is because it truly does feel like a legend. The archetypal story of good vs evil is done superbly in Ocarina, and no matter which version I’ve played, it always feels epic, heroic and legendary. I’ve seen many reviewers say that perhaps this version isn’t made for “us”, “us” being older gamers who were there from the beginning, however, I don’t agree; this legend belongs to us all, and I hope that when I’m long dead and gone, people will still be telling the legend of the Hero of Time.

1. It feels 3x faster than the original, because it is, 2. coupled with the incredible sound and music,3. upgraded visuals to the nth degree.. 4. And given the magic of the original

All of the above combined and this is the ultimate ocarina of time experience. Speechless...

I finished the game just now, and I just wish the game was handled a bit more.... grand? I think? Like we've already had a 1-to-1 remake with the 3DS version. Obviousy this Switch remake isn't 1-to-1, but it's still really close, and I do wish they had expanded that scope a bit more.

For what it was though.... I still really really enjoyed it, and I absolutely do not regret buying the game. Ocarina of Time is and always will be one of the best video games ever made, and this remake can count itself among that for sure. Just, because it played it a bit too safe, I can only give it a 9 out of 10 for that reason, even if I feel like it's a 10 out of 10 like the original was.

It's nice that it brings back that 90's nostalgia and is by far the prettiest Nintendo game ever. Also making me realize more of what the open world Zeldas need to incorporate in the future - a more detailed and narrative experience, and of course dungeons.

Having a great time playing it. But still it is a very safe remake. I would have loooooved if they had made it with the idea of "OoT but if it was made today", rather than basically a 1-to-1 remake. That woulda been a 10 for me.

Heck even if all they did was rebuild the combat and enemy AI from the ground up according to high modern standards to make combat and bosses wayyyy more interesting and more difficult, while also expanding some key areas, for example make Hyrule Field like >5x bigger and fill it with interesting places to explore and things to do so that it would be a whole little mini-world full of adventure, to bring the game closer to what an epic adventure game these days has, that woulda been a 10 for me.

So it's great cuz it's incredibly gorgeous OoT, but loses a bit from the disappointment of sticking exactly to what was cutting edge three decades ago rather than upgrading it (while keeping the same bones) into something that will wow people today. It's a safe and beautiful remake of a legendary game, so deserves a high score, but definitely a significant missed opportunity to do something more with it while they were going to the trouble of remaking the whole game.

Upon further reflection, I think another reason I loved playing this remake so much was because it showcases what I’m desperately missing - condensed, no nonsense, straight to the point gaming. As much as I genuinely adore BotW, Skyrim, the ancient Assassins Creeds, Super Mario Odyssey etc I’m so burned out on almost never ending games with an almost overabundance of things to do. Coming back to Ocarina of Time this weekend I had just finished playing Fenyx Immortals Rising and whilst I thought that another superb open world game, the tightly packed Ocarina felt like a breathe of fresh air and I missed this kind of game more than I’d realised. Perhaps moving forward game developers can come to some sort of middle ground, or even fully embrace the idea that not every game needs to last 50-100 hours plus to be incredible; there is so much room and I believe so much desire for these more contained experiences that have a definitive ending.

@TrogdorTheBurninator The game isn't open world, and that's what you're basically taking issue with. Breath of the Wild wasn't really an amazing experience for me. The game was primarily filler content to pad out play time, and put it on the player to make their own fun rather than giving the player actual meaningful or well designed content to play through. Tears of the Kingdom only further doubled down upon that approach.

The main game as an epic open world masterpiece that always tries to push the bounds of Zelda and gaming in general, a smaller more directed old style of 3D Zelda, and a classic style 2D Zelda. Three Zeldas every 10-12 years, but with each one very different.

#4056. Xbox Series X-BITE Alligator Console Returns With A New Video And Multiple New Images

The original trailer has already done over 1 million views

Earlier this week, Xbox unveiled a new custom console that we described as their most "insane" yet, and within just a few days, it's already racked up over 1 million views on the official Xbox YouTube channel.

There's a lot of hype around this thing, then, which explains why Xbox has teamed up with Complex and rapper Lil' Baby to reveal a new video and lots more images of the Xbox Series X-BITE in action.

For those who haven't been keeping up, the Xbox Series X-BITE is a functional console that sits inside of an alligator, and it appears to be inspired by GTA 6 (but for marketing reasons, Xbox can't say that!).

Here's a look at the new video, and we'll throw the new images below it:

There's apparently only one of these in the world, and it's been designed by John Nolan Studio - an animatronics specialist that has worked on some major Hollywood productions including Jurassic Park in the past.

The only way to win the Xbox alligator console is by entering the official sweepstakes, which is taking place across various social media platforms as we speak. Entries end on November 10th, so you haven't got long to enter.

We really hope the eventual winner ends up enjoying the system for themselves instead of flogging it for an insane amount of money, but we can't exactly blame them if they end up picking the latter option!

In any case, this is an extremely cool custom console, and maybe even the most elaborate in Xbox history.

News Microsoft Is Giving Away The Most Insane Xbox Series X Ever Created

Have you entered to try and win this thing? What do you think of it? Tell us in the comments down below.

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

#4055. There are no more Assassin's Creed remakes in development, because Ubisoft are focused on Hexe, Invictus and "projects you haven't heard about yet"

They're still updating Black Flag Resynced, however, and bringing NG+ to Valhalla

Ubisoft have announced that they aren't working on any more Assassin's Creed remakes for the moment, despite learning a "tremendous amount" from Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced. Instead, it's all shoulders to the wheel for a thrilling future that contains witches, a stronger sense of narrative cohesion, and possibly some kind of Assassin's Creed Smash Bros equivalent. In the shorter term, Ubisoft are still adding things to both Resynced and Assassin's Creed Valhalla.

The news comes as part of a fireside chat from Jean Guesdon, head of content. After offering libations to Assassin's Creed's new leadership team - in particular Martin Schelling, former Assassin's Creed: Revelations producer and nowadays, head of brand – he shares the results of a survey about whatpeople currently want from Assassin's Creed at large. Ubisoft's three takeaways are that players would like them to communicate more, work harder to shore up Assassin's Creed's "unique identity", and create "a more coherent narrative that respects and expands Assassin's Creed's lore."

All of which is basically telling us nothing, though I'm interested to hear thoughts from old AC stalwarts about where the frame story of Assassin vs Templar has gone off the rails. I feel like "incoherent" is AC's default state and a significant part of its charm. Ubisoft are going to do further closed-doors workshops about the future of the series with certain big cheeses in the AC fanbase, via Discord.

The post includes news of changes to existing Assassin's Creeds. Black Flag Resynced has just been updated with a New Game+ mode, a "nightmare" difficulty setting, some takedown animations, and some fresh cosmetics. Resynced's older/younger sibling Assassin's Creed Valhalla is also getting a New Game+ mode, out 5th November, which introduces a new optional progression system, more resources for upgrades, a new gear quality level, a stash system, and some cosmetics.

There's a section on Codename Invictus, Ubisoft's unrevealed multiplayer Assassin's Creed project, which had a closed playtest featuring a new prototype a few months ago. Ubisoft say people like the PvP, parkour, map verticality, and range of AC characters.

"One piece of feedback came through clearly though: players saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed," Guesdon writes. "The team spent the past months acting on it, and Invictus is now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions." I quite enjoyed Assassin's Creed's first efforts at multiplayer, in which players posed as NPCs on crowded maps, but as a Doubting Thomas, I also suspect Invictus is some kind of suffocating live service kraken. I suspect this is what the unnamed playtesters meant by wanting "more of the pillars".

I am more interested to hear about Codename Hexe, Ubisoft's other big forthcoming Creedojaunt, even though Clint Hocking is no longer working on it. It's reportedly a witch fable set during the time of the Holy Roman Empire. They'll be telling us more about that next year, Guesdon says.

Finally - well, apart from some flannel about the AC Netflix series and the series' 20th anniversary next year - there's a paragraph about remakes. "One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," Guesdon writes. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories. But don't mistake that for a closed door. Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back."

Some context for all this: Ubisoft recently made layoffs at Resynced studio Ubisoft Singapore, in the course of wider cost-cutting after an injection of funds from Tencent. In May, company boss Yves Guillemot told investors that the coming financial year would be a "low point", promising healthier returns from Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Ghost Recon by early 2029.

I didn't play Resynced, and I'm mixed on remakes at large. I like remakes when they are effectively brand new games that happen to be retelling a familiar story, and having fun with it: games like Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, which are in ferocious dialogue with the original. But remakes that are just about stuffing the mechanics into Unreal Engine 5 and grafting on some progression and crafting mechanics? It's just feeding ash to the fire. What's your mileage?

#4054. Petition to Save Mass Effect Dev BioWare to Be Considered by Canada's Government

A petition to save BioWare is set to be presented before the Canadian government.

The country's law states that any public petition with at least 500 signatures must be added to the House's agenda — and this fan-driven effort has amassed over 2,300 at the time of writing.

It argues that the Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer is "one of Canada's most important cultural exports to the world in the 21st century, selling tens of millions of units of their video games globally". It's a fair point.

"BioWare has been shuttered by its American parent company Electronic Arts, now owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners, and BioWare's closure represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada's cultural legacy," it rather pointedly continues.

Suggested solutions include providing the company with the "necessary" funding to secure its independence, while also, ideally, recovering IPs like Mass Effect and Dragon Age from EA.

News 'What a Loss for All of Us': Boss of Baldur's Gate 3 Maker Reacts to BioWare Closure

News EA Shutting Down RPG Dev BioWare, Next Mass Effect Game Cancelled

The petition concludes that the government should move to "protect Canadian businesses and cultural institutions from being dictated by American and foreign corporate interests."

The closing date for signatures is in March next year.

It's obviously a well-meaning petition driven by passionate fans — but as Eurogamer points out, there may not be much that the Canadian government can do, even if it agrees with the intent.

That's because, ultimately, BioWare — shuttered or not — is owned by EA. As are its aforementioned properties. Even if the country could fund some sort of deal, EA would still have to agree to the whole thing.

Still, the fact that this petition will be officially considered is pretty cool. For a long time, BioWare was considered a jewel in Canada's creative output — a bit like how CD Projekt Red has come to be viewed in Poland.

Do you think there's any genuine hope to this? Hop aboard the Normandy in the comments section below.

#4053. Helldivers 2 boss can "absolutely see" making a game parody of generative AI, but it would need to be "quirky" rather than "doom-laden"

Arrowhead's chief creative officer Johan Pilestedt can well imagine the Helldivers studio developing a videogame that satirises or parodies today's generative AI technology. The game in question wouldn't be a Helldivers project, however, and Pilestedt says it would need to be relatively upbeat, rather than an exercise in feverish despair. This seems like a tall order right now, at least while Tim Sweeney still has access to Twitter.

"AI has been worth parodying since the ‘80s, and I can absolutely see a game where you’re stuck in a world with an AI overlord that’s basically a deity," Pilestedt told me during an interview on the company's future. "But the Automatons already cover our robot enemy needs in Helldivers 2, so if we went there, it would be a new title, and we’d want to frame it in a quirky, fun way rather than a doom-laden one."

The aim to keep things light is consistent, of course, with how Helldivers approaches satire. "Not everyone gets it, but plenty of players love playing along with the joke," Pilestedt commented elsewhere in our chatathon, with regard to how Helldivers portrays fascism. "The humor doesn't hide the message, it delivers it."

While robotic, Helldivers 2's Automatons aren't a commentary on generative AI. They're broadly a spoof of Soviet Russia, red star imagery and all, if Soviet Russia had happened to be populated by Terminators. Based on the secessionist planet of Cyberstan, the Automatons are led by a group of Cyborgs who are waging war partly out of revenge for Super Earth's efforts to "euthanise" them. Still, perhaps there's scope to patch in more present-day parallels and upgrade the Automatons from cosy T-1000 analogues into something redolent of, say, Krafton's plans to use game data for unpiloted weapon systems.

Any satire of genAI Arrowhead make would need to reckon with the fact that Arrowhead appear open to making use of the technology, within limits. “I find that anything that is [an] AI-related debate in the games industry ends up being on both ends of the spectrum," Arrowhead CEO Shams Jorjani told The Game Business in an interview last year. "Either we have Square Enix executives talking about 77% being automated through QA, or we have developers who feel that... the very fabric of their being is being threatened and therefore all AI is bad AI. Maybe could it be that reality is somewhere in the middle?"

Jorjani contrasted fears about job losses to generative AI with less anxious reaction to older automation middleware such as Simplygon, while conceding that Simplygon isn't on the same "massive scale" as generative AI tools. He also stressed that "we need to make sure that we're not stealing people's intellectual property and rights".

Pilestedt didn't share his own opinions about generative AI during our conversation - in his defence, I didn't ask for them specifically. He did, however, talk about why Arrowhead's current unannounced project isn't Helldivers 3 - briefly, they don't want to "reset" the momentum of Helldivers 2.

It's become a long-running joke that Warhammer 40K Blood Angels fans keep getting ignored or neglected, but that could be due to change early next year.

In a surprise announcement on Warhammer Community, the team revealed that Codex: Blood Angels would be arriving as of spring 2027 alongside an undisclosed number of new Warhammer 40K models. Yes, this could end up being yet another snub with a character or two like before. But specific wording in the announcement makes me hope it'll be a bigger drop. The title promises "Big news for Blood Angels," after all. It also points out that "Alongside [the Codex] will be new miniatures." Miniatures, plural.

However, That same post provided a look at the first new model; the returning Sanguinary High Priest Corbulo, bearer of the Red Grail and seen strutting his stuff in the image above.

Although there haven't been any bespoke Blood Angels models for a while, the faction has been a big focus of the current 11th Edition. Indeed, they were the poster-army for the Armageddon box set (which you can currently grab for 15% less at Amazon).

I'll admit, I could be applying clown makeup to myself right now or injecting copious amounts of hopium. Especially because last edition offered crumbs and even the upcoming Christmas Blood Angels Battleforce (which has just been announced) was a very weak entry, even compared to other boxes dropping at the same time. But making such a song and dance about this new Blood Angels launch, and their prominence in the current Warhammer 40K edition, make me hope they'll enjoy the same treatment the Dark Angels got at the beginning of 10th Edition – new heroes and troops alike.

It won't just be Blood Angels enjoying reinforcements either; spring will apparently bring us new releases for "Xenos, Chaos, and non-Space Marine Imperial armies." Could that be when we'll receive the long-promised Steel Legion revamp?

For now, we'll just have to wait and see. As it stands, one of the last major launches of the year looks to be Kill Team: Armageddon and its kick-ass Legion of the Damned.

#4050. Rockstar developer union could end up over 1,600 workers strong and encompass nearly all UK staff below senior management, IWGB claim

Organisers say a successful vote would create "the biggest recognised union in the UK games sector"

As we've previously covered, a vote on recognition of a union made up of UK-based Rockstar Games devs is set to take place around GTA 6's console launch on November 19th. The Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB) union, whom the Rockstar staff are working with in their efforts to organise, have now revealed just how many workers the Rockstar could end up encompassing if the recognition vote is successful. It's not a small number.

As reported by Game File, when asked to put a number on their claim that the vote could result in "the biggest recognised union in the UK games sector", the IWGB said that the union’s bargaining unit would be made up of more than 1,600 workers. That, according to the union, is nearly everyone at Rockstar's UK studios below the director level. The director level's typically corpospeak for senior management, or the point at which you go from regular staff to the lowest rungs of the exec ladder which leads all the way up to the biggest of gold-plated desks.

Naturally, this UK Rockstar union won't include Rockstar staff based in other studios across the world, including the US and India. Recent reporting from Bloomberg cited Rockstar's total staff number as being over 4,700 people in 12 places across the globe.

The UK union recognition votes will be held from November 12th, a week before GTA 6's console launch, and November 26th.

"For me, this vote comes down to ensuring employees at Rockstar get honesty and openness surrounding the decisions that affect them," Rockstar Game Workers Union Committee Member Shanti Easton-Steel said in a press release issued by IWBG earlier this week. "When management choices are kept hidden, we can’t properly address issues like the gender pay gap, the uneven and ever-changing policies on overtime pay, or the concerns many co-workers hold around job security post-release."

Also set to come to a head around the time GTA 6 plops onto consoles is the employment tribunal which has seen Rockstar and the IWGB butt heads over the former's decision to fire 34 mostly UK-based staffers last year. Rockstar have accused the fired staff of risking the leaking of confidential info while posting on a Discord server set up by union organisers. The IWGB have accused Rockstar of being motivated by a desire to union bust.

#4048. Forza Horizon 6's New City Life Update Includes Multiple Halo & Xbox Freebies

Unlock Master Chief, liveries and the Xbox IKEA Prop Pack!

Yesterday marked the long-awaited arrival of Forza Horizon 6's City Life update, which adds two new permanent race routes in Tokyo City amongst other things, and there are even some Xbox and Halo-related freebies tucked in!

In terms of Halo, it's said that everyone will soon be getting a free 2025 GR GT Prototype livery via the Message Centre celebrating the franchise along with Xbox's 25th anniversary. We haven't come across this yet, although we did get a separate Master Chief livery for the Urus Lamborghini as well.

Meanwhile, Master Chief himself will become available as a character model in the Week 2 Photo Challenge.

"Additionally, join us in celebrating 25 Years of XBOX and Halo with a special livery on the 2025 GR GT Prototype (to be sent to all players via Message Center) and The Master Chief Outfit unlockable in the Week 2 Photo Challenge of the Festival Playlist."

Beyond this, they've also added an IKEA Prop Pack containing items from the recent real-life collaboration with Xbox that you can use to decorate your custom garages, so that's a neat little addition.

As for the more meaty stuff, you'll find 3 new-to-Horizon cars in the Festival Playlist, while the two new race routes arrive in the form of the Edo Circuit Road Race and Shuto Charge Street Race.

Most of this is available to check out in Forza Horizon 6 right now, although as mentioned, the Halo livery for the GR GT Prototype and Master Chief character skin haven't arrived just yet. Plenty to be getting on with in the meantime!

#4047. Rumour: Data Found In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time May Hint At Master Quest DLC

One of our main bugbears with Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 – as incredible as it is – is that it's overall quite a breezy experience for those already familiar with the original or 3DS release.

As such, we thought it might beneficial if Nintendo were to include a more difficult mode, whether it be a simple Hero Mode in which enemies deal more damage, or perhaps even a port of the reworked Master Quest mode from the GameCube and 3DS.

Our prayers may (emphasis on the 'may') soon be answered, as a post from MrCheeze on BlueSky reveals that data found in Ocarina of Time may be hinting at some sort of Master Quest content. You'll see in the image below that many of the lines of data include 'MQ' next to the title 'DodongoCavern'.

MrCheeze has also provided more information in a follow-up post, stating "Couple strings in the exefs as well giving some context (HasMQ, IsMQModeExist, NewGameMQ, ReleaseMQ)".

So does this mean Master Quest is on the way? Potentially. We're not quite ready to put money on it, but it would certainly make sense for Nintendo to include it as part of a DLC expansion, whether free or paid.

Almost all first-party Nintendo games these days include some sort of post-launch DLC, so we've no reason to believe Ocarina of Time would be any different. As ever, though, do take all of this with a pinch of salt.

In a recent interview with IGN, producer Eiji Aonuma stated " I don't think that we would announce anything specific at this time" when asked whether Master Quest was considered for the Switch 2 remake.

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

Welcome back to Conformity Gate. With Stranger Things Day sending us all back to the Upside Down today, Sony has the headphones to pair with that world-saving Walkman. The brand has just announced a Stranger Things edition of the new MDR-3R wired headphones, now available with bold red cushions (and a black set included in the box). The $79 / £59 Stranger Things variant bumps up the price of the new release a little (the standard model starts at $59 / £49) but maintains a style fit for Hawkins.

The Sony MDR-3R headphones are being described as "Newtro" by the brand, combining more modern audio handling (and a USB-C connection) with the instantly recognizable retro aesthetic. Sony has faithfully reconstructed the MDR-3 design, with that skinny band, chunky silver driver plate, and simple design. If we ever needed another reason to start running up that hill, this is it.

The new Sony MDR-3Rs are still waiting to go live on the brand's own site, though notifications are available if you want to be one of the first in the line. It's worth noting that the red-cushion Stranger Things version is a limited edition, so keep that refresh button warm.

So what does the Stranger Things edition bring to its higher price tag? It's a subtle one. The blue / orange cushion color options of the standard model are replaced with a deep Upside Down red and black pairing with a Stranger Things logo stamped at the top of the headband.

If you're going for the full '80s aesthetic, you'd be better off with the orange base option, saving yourself some cash in the process. If you're going like-for-like with Max herself, you'll need the limited edition to get access to those black pads.

The headphones themselves are constructed from a lightweight aluminum and stainless steel, powered by that USB-C connection for a charge-free experience, and still feature an inline remote with an integrated microphone for media control and calls.

Sony says it's kept the MDR-3R sound profile as close to the original as possible, while still elevating sound with some more modern features. That open-back design is still going to give your music plenty more breathing space, but the brand has extended both lower and upper ranges for a more dynamic quality.

While the absence of that ninth episode still continues to hurt, at least we've got some tunes to see us through. Plus, with Maya Hawke joining the Magic: The Gathering movie there's still plenty from the series stars in the works.

#4045. Sony's Killing This Ratchet & Clank Game Before It Even Comes Out

One of PlayStation's mobile games is shutting up shop, and it's doing so before it's managed to launch globally.

You may recall Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, a mobile multiplayer game set within Insomniac Games' beloved sci-fi universe.

It's been quietly making progress with soft launches in specific countries, and was gearing up for a proper, global launch sometime soon. However, developer Oh BiBi has today announced its plans to cease development and close the whole thing down.

The official website for the game has been updated with a notice of the shutdown.

"We've made the difficult decision to cease development of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble," the statement reads. "The final planned update will be rolling out November 6th, 2026, and the app will be removed from stores on November 21st, 2026."

Players who already have the game can carry on playing through to 1st May 2027, which is the date when the game's servers will permanently go offline. After this point, the game will no longer be playable.

In-app purchases have been removed, and content that was once premium is now available for free, or can be earned through normal play.

The game did release in some countries, including the UK and Canada, as part of a soft launch period before a planned worldwide launch. Back in July, people were invited to pre-register in preparation for the full release, but that will now sadly not be happening.

Ranger Rumble is a competitive multiplayer arena shooter of sorts with cartoonish visuals, various modes to play, and live service elements like time-limited events and seasonal rewards.

On the App Store, the game has a user score of 4.2 (out of 5) after 93 ratings, while it has a 4.4 score after more than 2,000 ratings on Google Play Store.

It's a shame to see the game go down the pan before it really got a proper chance.

Sony does have one or two other mobile games in the pipeline, including Horizon Steel Frontiers, in development at NCSOFT. Hopefully it fares better.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a remake masterpiece, but takes one leap too far

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I'm on a roll as I enter Dodongo's Cavern, the fiery labyrinth and second dungeon in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Despite plenty of tweaks and changes, muscle memory of my previous playthroughs has kept me on task – adult wallet acquired, deku nuts on lock, Hylian Shield strapped on my back. Then, I walk forward a few steps towards ledges above flaming pools of lava and immediately faceplant, my poor little elfin boy immediately set aflame. Yes, Navi, I need some hearts.

Perhaps the biggest gameplay change in Ocarina of Time remake compared to the Nintendo 64 original is swapping the auto-jump to a manual button press. Previously, running toward an edge would have the green-garbed Link always jump from the furthest point possible. Now, I have to press a button to do it myself. Great. And why don't I rock up to my local pizza place to bake my own pie next time I order, too? While I see Super Mario 64 challenge runs completing that game without jumping at all, I've been doomed to tap the jump-button in the Zelda equivalent endlessly.

I'm exaggerating, but only a bit. There are actually loads of times in which the manual control of Link's hops, and how reactive all his moves are in a world that feels utterly teeming with life, helps this remake buzz with a new energy. Small layout changes to early areas add a smidge more naturalistic verticality to some zones, while scampering through towns and mantling ledges simply makes navigation of the overworld much more swish.

Still, it's in the more traditional Zelda dungeon exploration and challenges that I stumble. I'm so used to routing my way through these dangerous areas by pointing myself in the right direction and chaining together auto-jumps that I find myself forgetting or mistiming the input to go early or roll by mistake and end up going splat. This is very embarrassing to admit as a big platformer fan who usually wastes no time click-clacking the stick to do side somersaults up forbidden pathways. Something about having to press the jump button in Ocarina of Time is vexing me. And I'm far from the only one.

In part, it's because I have played these games before. These jumps are deeply familiar to me, designed without a manual jump button at all, only to now have the need foisted upon them. It's not like Elden Ring where the addition of a more natural jump compared to Dark Souls was incorporated into its level design approach from the ground-up.

While the position of, say, the pond with the platforms in Kokiri Village may have been adjusted, the sequence is the same as the original. Except, now, you have to press another button the whole time while doing it rather than thinking only about steering.

I'm being picky, and a bit of a grumbler – I do agree with Anna's 5-star Ocarina of Time remake review. This is an exceptional overhaul. But, it's not as if the concept of a jump-button was completely alien to the N64 development team – the original game was intentionally designed not to need a jump button. It's not like they just forgot to include it.

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

In fact, I'd say more isn't always better – like a sloppy, delicious-looking burger with too many toppings to get your jaw around. For me, some of the joy of revisiting classic Zelda is the simplicity of control that allows depth elsewhere. It's not as if auto-jumping was an N64 limitation, the traversal mechanic having remained in the series all the way through to Breath of the Wild.

Many of the best Zelda games, as a result, make fantastic use of auto-jump without the need for manual jump at all – Wind Waker, Twilight Princess, all the rest. In Breath of the Wild it made sense with the design shift to the open world, freeform focused exploration, away from tight dungeon design. Ocarina of Time remake isn't so different that this fundamental control choice suddenly needs an overhaul.

I'm not fuming it's here, but I'm a bit baffled at the dedication to manual jump. If you're going to add it in, why not keep auto-jump as a toggle or additional option? After all, the Ocarina of Time remake dev team explicitly kept the classic jump-attack and rolling options alongside their modern control versions. Granted, some reworked sections now require manual jumping – climbing up a bit of wall into the Hyrule Castle gardens, for example, which I quite like – but why does that mean I also can't auto-jump when I run at an edge?

Largely, Ocarina of Time remake is a more well-considered overhaul than I had first feared. Over the last few years, I've been finding remakes broadly very hit and miss. Loads of small tweaks feel dialled in to perfection, from the exact amount of luscious detail to enemy animations making combat feel more reactive – all while respecting much of the core design that made Ocarina of Time such a classic. But, when I'm tumbling into the lava because I forgot that not all original design concepts are quite so revered as others at the altar of strapping on more game mechanics, well, it burns a little.

Time marches on. Check out our upcoming Switch 2 releases for more adventures on the horizon!

#4043. Video: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Side-By-Side Graphics Comparison (Switch 2, 3DS, N64)

Zelda: Ocarina of Time returned this week on the Switch 2 and it looks better than ever. If you are wondering just much of a facelift it's had since the 2011 outing, and the original N64 hit, you might want to check out this side-by-side comparison video.

YouTube channel ElAnalistDeBits has now released a "final graphics comparison" which takes a closer look at the character models, environments, physics, the many locations in the game, and much more.

If you are wondering about the performance, the remake on Switch 2 runs at 60fps. In comparison, the original N64 outing ran at 20fps. And as for the resolution, this new remake ranges from 1080p to 1440p in docked, and 720p to 1080p in handheld (via Digital Foundry).

In our review of the Ocarina of Time remake, we noted it was the most visually stunning work Nintendo has ever released:

"Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is a stellar reimagining of the original, one that completely revamps the experience with stunning visuals, modernised gameplay, and vastly improved audio. Despite some minor blemishes, this is comfortably the most visually stunning work Nintendo has ever put out, and it’s unquestionably the best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time."

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

Review The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake - One of Nintendo's Best-Looking Games Ever

#4042. 11 Bit Studios Signs Deal To Release Three 'Day One' Xbox Game Pass Titles In 2027

We've already heard about many titles coming to Xbox Game Pass in 2027, including the likes of Stranger Than Heaven and Fable in the first couple of months, and now we know that 11 Bit Studios will be joining the lineup next year too.

The publisher (and developer in some cases) behind such games as Frostpunk 2, The Alters and Moonlighter 2 has officially entered into an agreement with Microsoft to release three upcoming games on Xbox Game Pass.

Here's the confirmation, as shared on social media:

The deal unfortunately doesn't mention what the three games will be, but confirms they're from the "publishing portfolio" (so not necessarily developed by them), and are "scheduled for release in 2027".

Plans for 11 Bit Studios are mostly unknown at the moment, but they are confirmed to be working on a new version of Frostpunk called Frostpunk 1886, along with a psychological horror game called Trainwatch and a narrative-driven survival farming simulator known as Crop. Who knows whether any of these will make the cut for Game Pass though.

Let's wait and see! We've had a lot of fun with a whole bunch of 11 Bit Studios titles on Xbox Game Pass over the years, and these three upcoming titles should prove excellent additions to the service in 2027 - whatever they may be.

#4040. These 8+ PS5 Games Will Be Delisted in November and December 2026

The end of the year is always a prime time for PS5 game delistings and server closures, but fortunately we’re being spared a large list this year.

There are about eight titles with impending changes you need to be aware of, so here’s the full list:

Sony game Destruction AllStars will go completely offline on 25th November, following some alterations earlier in the year.

This will render most of the single player content unplayable, outside of a few arcade challenges, although the platform holder says your overall experience may be affected in those too.

In-game purchases will then be removed from Synduality: Echoes of Ada, the Bandai Namco live service shooter. This is the beginning of the publisher repurposing the game as a single player-only experience, with more changes planned in 2027.

PSVR2 MMO Zenith: Nexus will go offline on 18th December, and then the end of the year brings a slew of delistings, primarily from publisher GameMill.

This is due to licenses expiring for franchises like Avatar: The Last Airbender and Street Outlaws. If you purchase these games before they’re removed, they’ll remain in your library.

While it never officially released, PlayStation fans may want to pay attention to the impending closure of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, which will be removed from mobile storefronts on 21st November.

One final thing to note is that 2K Sports will disable the online servers of NBA 2K25 on 31st December, but single player modes will remain.

That’s the full breakdown of everything being delisted in November and December 2026, then. I’ll update should any other announcements be made before the end of the year.

Is there anything here you’re going to miss? Let me know below.

As the Editor of Push Square, Sammy has over 15 years of experience analysing the world of PlayStation, from PS3 through PS5 and everything in between. He’s an expert on PS Studios and industry matters, as well as sports games and simulators. He also enjoys RPGs when he has the time to dedicate to them, and is a bit of a gacha whale.

#4039. Black Panther 2 is still Marvel's best passing of the torch – so I hope Shuri gets to shine in Avengers: Doomsday

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

On the road to Avengers: Doomsday, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever remains Marvel's best passing of the torch

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Shuri was never supposed to be the Black Panther. In 2020, Chadwick Boseman, who portrayed T'Challa with so much regal gravitas, died at the age of 43. In the terrible aftermath, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever was released – a beautiful entry in the MCU that functions both as a deeply loving tribute to Boseman and an emotional passing of the torch to Letitia Wright's Shuri.

It's this context that makes Black Panther: Wakanda Forever such an extraordinary accomplishment. Not only is it a genuinely thrilling chapter in the MCU, but it also pulls off the tricky task of handing over the mantle in a way that feels respectful and natural to the characters involved, while honoring the real Boseman. It doesn't shy away from this reality, instead choosing to tell a story that focuses heavily on Shuri's raw grief and her complicated journey to stepping up as her nation's protector.

Now, Shuri is set to return in Avengers: Doomsday, standing alongside other Marvel titans like Chris Hemsworth's Thor and the original X-Men. I just hope that, among the stacked cast, Shuri gets her chance to shine – because she's earned it.

Wakanda Forever begins with T'Challa dying from a mystery illness. Despite her super-genius intellect, Shuri is powerless against this invisible enemy and unable to synthesize a new heart-shaped herb, and so T'Challa dies. Shuri, who idolized her big brother, is devastated – and, after a time-skip of a year, she is still struggling with her all-encompassing grief, which is making her as angry as she is heartbroken.

Welcome to Road to Doomsday, GamesRadar+'s weekly MCU rewatch series. Over 15 weeks, we'll be revisiting each Marvel movie and TV show on Disney's list of essential movies to watch ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, sharing our thoughts upon rewatching and deciphering what we can learn about the next Marvel mega-event from each entry. Why not relive some MCU highlights and watch along with us?

It's this raw emotion that makes Shuri's journey to becoming a fully fledged hero so compelling. Shuri, very understandably, does not want to become the Black Panther. It doesn't even cross her mind. Instead, she has the incredibly human reaction of simply wanting to grieve. But in the Marvel universe, nobody has any breathing space for long, and the arrival of Namor and the threat of CIA intervention over Vibranium pushes Shuri back into the fray. It's when the situation spirals out of control, and Namor kills her mother, Queen Ramonda, that Shuri finally returns to attempting to reconstruct the heart-shaped herb.

As a showdown with Killmonger in the Ancestral Plane demonstrates, though, Shuri is not solely motivated by an altruistic desire to be a hero: she wants revenge. Her anger and pain at the loss of T'Challa have been exacerbated by the murder of her mother, resulting in a furious grief that threatens to plunge Wakanda into an endless war with its underwater neighbours. It's a natural breaking point in her struggle to deal with so much loss, and sets Shuri's arc apart from the rise to greatness of other MCU heroes in its messy, intense vulnerability and pain.

Ultimately, though, Shuri, movingly encouraged by the spirit of Ramonda, chooses peace by sparing Namor's life and putting an end to the fighting between Wakanda and Talokan. This triumphant finish clears the way, allowing Shuri to finally process her grief – and even meet her nephew, T'Challa II. Her story in the film ends with a quiet moment on the beach, burning her mourning clothes, letting go of the painful past in order to face a more hopeful future.

Shuri's journey is not easy, and it's not one she even wanted – mirroring the awful real-life circumstances that led to the storyline. In this anguish is a beautiful evolution, powered by a standout performance from Wright, that brings Shuri from the fun, kid sister sidekick to the Black Panther herself. This passing of the torch is so effective because it truly means something, both within the MCU and in real life, and it gifts Shuri with boundless potential.

It was announced at SDCC that Shuri will soon be passing on the mantle herself, this time to T'Challa II. The Long Walk star David Jonsson will play the character, though how it will all work out is unclear at the moment, since Jonsson is much older than the young T'Challa II at the end of Wakanda Forever. ("In this next film, he grows up, comes of age, and we had to find an incredible actor," director Ryan Coogler shared on stage.)

This passing of the torch is so effective because it truly means something

Hopefully, then, Shuri gets her chance to shine in Avengers: Doomsday before surrendering the mantle. This is her first opportunity to truly spread her wings as the Black Panther after Wakanda Forever, and, with such a stacked cast, there's every risk Shuri might fall by the wayside – which would be a huge mistake, after how far she has come. She can be glimpsed in the trailers so far, though sadly not for very long.

Before Avengers: Doomsday, Spider-Man: No Way Home proved the best Marvel event movies put character first

But Wright may have already inadvertently let slip that she's part of the Avengers: Secret Wars cast, which would mean we have one more chance after Doomsday to see her in all her power before Jonsson takes over in Black Panther 3. What might happen in Secret Wars heavily depends on Doomsday, of course, but this duo of blockbuster event films offers the perfect chance to bring Shuri's MCU story to a meaningful close, paying off the emotional set-up of Wakanda Forever.

Shuri was never supposed to be the Black Panther, but she has more than proved how capable she is of being Wakanda's protector – and I hope Doomsday gives her the chance to truly show it.

Black Panther: Wakanda Forever is available to stream now on Disney Plus, ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday on December 18.

#4038. Splendid Junji Ito-inspired RPG World of Horror is now 20% more horrible, thanks to a free PC update with extra gods, locations, and wounds

This hole was already made for me, but now it's a fair bit wider and deeper

Excellent apocalypse RPG World of Horror has just received a sizeable free update, As Below So Above, adding no less than two Old Godly invasions for you to identify and thwart. One of these additional cosmic disasters involves four cults summoning their fave abominations at the same time. I picture them forming a shaky barbershop quartet on the skyline, while stamping the streets to mush. Damn it, Ath-Yolazsth – you're leading again!

Also in As Below So Above: more "enemies, mysteries, characters, items, spells, curses, and injuries", together with "a large batch of quality-of-life features and bug fixes". I can only applaud the vicious disconnect of listing "injuries" alongside "quality-of-life". These will be the most polished and ergonomic grievous wounds you've ever had! The experience will flow like your gushing blood!

This is the Junji Ito-inspired game's largest update yet, according to developers panstasz and publishers Ysbryd. It makes the game 20% bigger, though surely no mere percentage can ever encapsulate the creatures and forces that slumber on the other side of the mortal veil.

"Two never-before-seen manifestations of the Old Gods raise the stakes," explains the press release. "IKT-YOSIS, THE FIRST NIGHTMARE, sleeps in a gargantuan chamber beneath the mountains. With each ritual performed to wake him, the world above slowly reshapes itself and brings strange weather with it." You'll need to keep tabs on forecasts, if you want to get ahead of the elements. As for "THE WAR FOR SHIOKAWA", this "adds an extra level of terror, with four cults summoning their eldritch masters simultaneously to plunge the town into pure evil."

It's just as well there are three new puny human protagonists to continue the battle against these cyclopean trouble-makers: Kiriko, who knows her way around a Tarot deck, Satoshi, a seasoned hiker, and Makoto, a school AV club member. You'll also be able to enlist 10 additional allies and learn about them care of a reworked conversation system, which trips at random between investigations.

There's a new location, the Mountains, alongside 60 extra events, 19 enemies, three challenges, and 30 items. And let's not forget the Scenario Mode, which plays host to self-contained yarns set before the main game. The first of these Worldlets of Horror is a hunt for three students lost in the woods, with a variety of endings.

Lots of numbers! And while much of this may break your mind, none of it will break your mods. There's a new modding system that's backwards compatible with everything made for the 1.0 version.

Unfamiliar with World of Horror? Here is Alice Bee's review (RPS in peace): "Repetitive combat in World Of Horror can't entirely mar a unique, stylish and layered horror adventure that makes you want to play more the more that you play."

#4037. Digital Foundry Delivers Its Tech Verdict On Stellar Blade's Switch 2 Port

Stellar Blade also arrived on the Switch 2 this week, and it's been positively received so far. Here on Nintendo Life, we gave it a score of seven out of ten, and although there are some technical drawbacks, Eve's outing stands tall on the hybrid platform.

The team at Digital Foundry has now delivered its tech review of the Unreal Engine 4 title, and while it's no "tour de force", it does translate to a "better than expected Switch 2 port", with what's described as an experience with "gentler compromises" than many more recent titles.

"Technically, it's not a tour de force either, with more conservative visual technology that doesn't leverage current gen hardware like many other high budget titles, but that does translate to a better than expected Switch 2 port, with gentler compromises than many more recent titles. Not everything survives intact, but the game's visual character isn't disrupted by the excision of key lighting systems or anything like that. Instead, players can expect a range of more iterative asset downgrades, some of which only really stand out in head-to-heads."

As for frame generation, on Switch 2, Digital Foundry says it's "not a bad choice considering the CPU and GPU limits of the console", but in the case of Stellar Blade, a "40fps targeting option" may have offered a better experience than the 60fps output with frame gen on. You can also turn frame gen "off" and the game will hover around the 40fps mark.

Overall, though, Stellar Blade is summed up as a "reasonable" and "playable experience" on Nintendo's new system. You can get the full rundown in the video above. There's also a demo on the eShop, and you find out more about how it performs in our review here on Nintendo Life:

#4036. Hideo Kojima Is 'Inventing A New Medium' - Bill Skarsgård Shares Why Starring In Xbox's PHYSINT Is A 'Big Deal'

"I think Kojima is a pioneer, and keeps going out to untrodden waters"

Hideo Kojima always brings a certain sense of mystery and allure to his work, as is currently the case with the OD KNOCK and PHYSINT projects. For quite some time, speculation over who would star in the latter threw all sorts of crazy names into the mixer, before Kojima revealed that Pennywise and Dune actor Bill Skarsgård had got the job.

Skarsgård recently appeared on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, where he spoke about how working with Hideo Kojima is a "big deal" for him. He also admitted that he grew up playing all the Metal Gear Solid games and is a big fan of Kojima's process.

"I played every single one [Metal Gear Solid], at least the ones on platform. So, I was very enamoured by him and the sort of the mythology or the universes that he creates, but also the sort of mystique and allure about him as well."

As the actor continued to praise the Metal Gear creator, Skarsgård seemed to specifically be impressed by Kojima's fluent knowledge of filmmaking despite being a video game developer. He even recalled a moment where he asked Kojima if he would ever make a film:

"[Kojima] is an auteur, but he's a video game auteur. He's fluent in filmmaking, in film, and in cinema. I remember at one point, way back 20 years ago, there was talk about doing a Metal Gear Solid movie, and, is gonna Hideo gonna direct it? I asked him, 'would you ever do a film?' and he's like 'no'. At this point, what he's doing is inventing a new medium."

Skarsgård touched briefly on his performance capture in PHYSINT and suggested he's working on eight hours of narrative storytelling.

"What we're gonna do is eight hours worth of narrative, right? But it's also an entire universe that you play, so it truly is quite literally world building. But now with technology, we're getting closer and closer to something that's photorealistic, but it's also interactive when you play it. I think he's a pioneer, and keeps going out to untrodden waters."

PHYSINT is a return to tactical espionage for Kojima since departing Konami and Metal Gear Solid in 2015. We're very excited to see what he's been cooking up with Bill and the rest of the cast when we eventually learn more. Xbox has also remained fairly quiet on how PHYSINT fits into Microsoft's exclusivity plans.

#4035. Guide: GTA 6 Release Times and Preload: When Can You Start Playing?

Probably the most anticipated game of all time, GTA 6 is now less than two weeks away. As the launch draws closer, we're covering everything you need to know about its PS5 launch, including preload options and release times. In this GTA 6 guide, we cover the GTA 6 release times and preload.

On this page: GTA 6 Release Times and Preload: When Can You Start Playing?

Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will officially be playable from midnight on 19th November in your local time zone. As such, the game will unlock and be available first in New Zealand. If you preload the game, you'll be able to start playing GTA 6 as soon as it hits midnight on 19th November where you live.

If you pre-order the game, GTA 6 will be available to preload from 10th November. This is nine days before the game comes out, and was just brought forward two days by Rockstar.

Pre-ordering digitally means your preload should start automatically on PS5 as soon as it becomes available. The boxed physical version, which is just a code in the box, comes out on 12th November, the same day. You can redeem the code inside the case and start preloading the digital version of GTA 6 if you buy the game this way.

Rockstar has now officially confirmed the GTA 6 file size on PS5, and what you'll need to download, is 212GB. This is one of the biggest downloads and installs on console in history, and will probably only get bigger through patches and the addition of GTA Online.

GTA 6 will unlock and be playable in New Zealand first, as it's located in one of the furthest along timezones. The chances are New Zealand is further along in the day compared to wherever you live in the world, so yes, New Zealand will be the first to gain access to GTA 6.

Because of this, there's been a rising trend in people creating New Zealand PSN account to play games as soon as possible. This can be done with GTA 6 too, but you'll need to set up a fresh New Zealand PSN account and buy the game through its PS Store.

When you have done, you'll be able to play GTA 6 a few hours ahead of other countries like the USA. Keep in mind, though, that you can't transfer your save data from the New Zealand account you set up to your normal profile.

GTA 6 is available digitally on the PS Store, or in a basic physical version that ships without a disc. The latter provides a code in the box that you redeem on the PS Store to get the digital version.

The two PS5 digital versions on offer are: Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition.

Ultimate Edition / Ultimate Edition Upgrade Contents:

Rockstar is only selling GTA 6 in a digital format; you can't buy the game on a physical disc in any way. Even the version you buy in retail shops or from online retailers won't contain a disc. Instead, the actual GTA 6 box will have a code inside you can use to download the game. There's no version with a physical disc of any kind.

Rockstar has now confirmed a GTA 6 map will be made available, but it won't be included in the physical versions like for previous games. Instead, a physical GTA 6 map will be put on the official Rockstar store for $0.99. Or, it'll be included for free in all other purchases from the storefront.

Have you pre-ordered GTA 6, and will you be staying up to play at midnight? Let us know in the comments below.

#4034. EA execs choosing Star Wars Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect 5 was the main factor in BioWare's demise, according to report

Corporate chair shuffling and the Mass Effect studio's recent struggles may also have played roles

The postmortem on BioWare, following their shuttering by EA this month, points to the publisher's preference to back Star Wars Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect 5 as the main factor in the demise of the beloved RPG developer. That's according to Bloomberg, who also report that a couple of other factors likely also had some influence.

The Bloomberg report paints EA's position as being one of a company caught between spending a bunch of money on a Star Wars shooter-shaped rock and a hard place with a sign that read Mass Effect 5. Disney reportedly swooped in to offer the publishers the opportunity to make Star Wars Battlefront 3 around the time EA were, as a result of being saddled with debt as part of the leveraged buyout which saw the Saudi government and private equity take them over, looking to not to spend as much cash.

So, Star Wars and Mass Effect became a decision of whether Star Wars or Mass Effect would be the better bet to stick projected hundreds of millions of dollars on. The suits, quelle surprise really, went for the series that currently sits just below powerhouse money-maker Winnie the Pooh on Wikipedia's list of the highest-grossing media franchises. Battlefront 3's development reportedly hasn't even kicked off yet, but it's got that safe and predictable big name to it, and will be a shooter to nestle among EA's treasured flotilla of gun and ball games, rather than an RPG.

Bloomberg add that that BioWare's well-documented up and down record with game releases since Mass Effect: Andromeda began a skid which Anthem only made worse and Dragon Age: The Veilguard couldn't arrest also played a role. Potentially also in the mix was some corporate chair and nameplate switching among EA's execs this summer, which saw EA Sports-linked suits David Tinson and Cam Weber promoted while reported BioWare advocate Laura Miele was sidelined via promotion from overseeing EA's non-sports studios to a gig based around helping big boss Andrew Wilson pursue "strategic growth opportunities beyond EA's core business".

For what it's worth, an EA spokesperson told Bloomberg the company "collectively" decided to shoot BioWare into space "following months of planning, review, and analysis, including careful consideration of evolving business conditions, industry dynamics, and our long-term priorities".

And so, BioWare's body has been sent to the stars, while Respawn and DICE look set to make Battlefront 3. There is a bit of depressing irony in EA deciding to go for the perceived safe bet of a big name licensed game over taking some risk on a game that'd come without Disney as a rights-holding middleman. This is, after all, the company which in 2022 ditched governing body Fifa as the namesake and licensing partner of their very successful football games, choosing the risk of going it alone with a lesser brand EA would have more direct control over and ownership of rather than sticking with an established big name juggernaut.

Then again, you could probably call EA's soccer games something like 'Hey, you, person reading this: the (insert year here) football game you're looking at thinks your face is ugly and your haircut's stupid' and they'd still fly off the shelves.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Physint star Bill Skarsgård was "very enamored" by Hideo Kojima growing up, and at this point he's far from the only Hollywood actor to feel that way.

In an appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, host Josh Horowitz asks Skarsgård about his recently announced collab with Kojima, after he was announced as the lead of his upcoming Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor Physint back in September.

Skarsgård says "that's a big deal for me," and when asked if he's a gamer, he notes, "specifically the Metal Gear Solid games," adding that he "played every single" game from the PS1 title to "the last one" (presumably Metal Gear Solid 5, I can't imagine he means Survive).

He adds, "I was very enamored by him and the sort of mythology in the universes that he creates," adding, "I was really into it growing up."

Skarsgård calls Kojima an "auteur," saying "he's fluent in film making" while recalling word "way back 20 years ago" that there was talk of a Metal Gear Solid movie and the question of whether Kojima himself will direct it. Skarsgård remembers thinking, "I can't wait to see him transition it to film," but notes that "now it's gotten to the point where I asked him 'would you ever do a film?' and he's like 'no.'"

"At this point what he's doing is he's inventing a new medium," Skarsgård adds. "What we're going to do is going to be eight hours worth of narrative, right? But it's also an entire universe that you play." He calls what Kojima is doing "quite literally world building." As for Kojima himself, Skarsgård calls him a "pioneer" and says "he keeps going out into untreaded waters."

Speaking of upcoming Hideo Kojima games, Skarsgård's comments come months after OD star Hunter Schafer called the developer a "genius," with her OD co-star Sophia Lillis similarly being a fan of his games.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

This could also be our first hint of the type of game Physint is going to be, as he mentions "eight hours worth of narrative." This could be in theory a hint at the game following a format similar to the classic games in the series, with Metal Gear Solid 4 having nine hours of cutscenes. But then again, it could easily be taking the form of Metal Gear Solid 5 or Death Stranding where there's a whole lot of gameplay between those cutscenes, so maybe it's not a massive hint after all.

Hideo Kojima says Physint is "quite different" from Metal Gear: "I want plenty of new ideas and a different kind of spy action."

#4032. Nintendo's Bill Trinen Explains Why Ocarina Of Time Is The Perfect Place To Start In The Zelda Universe

If you're in a position where you've never actually played a Zelda game before, Nintendo's Bill Trinen just wants to let you know Ocarina of Time is the "perfect place" to start.

Although this comment just happens to line up with the arrival of the Switch 2 remake, Nintendo's VP of Player & Product Experience really is convinced this is the best game to begin with, as it's a "foundational story", where the player is taught everything they need to know about the world and characters.

Here's what he had to say at the remake's launch event in San Francisco this week:

Bill Trinen: "This is the perfect place for your first Zelda game, because you are gonna learn everything that there is about the world and the characters that will serve sort of as the foundation for all the others, all the games that came after.

"This game is sort of a really foundational story for the lore of the Legend of Zelda. It really tells the story of Link and his journey becoming a hero. It tells the story of Link and his connection to Zelda and their relationship with Ganondorf. And overall, it communicates kind of what is at the moral core of is all the series, which is the idea that wisdom and courage combined can overcome power."

There will likely be more eyes than ever on the Zelda series in 2027, when the live-action film arrives in cinemas in April. So Ocarina of Time truly is a fantastic entry point into the Zelda universe if you haven't played the games before. The remake on Switch 2 also updates the gameplay and mechanics to offer a more accessible experience.

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

"That's one of the most exciting things for us"

#4031. Xbox's New PC App Update Is Impressive, Even If There's A Few Teething Problems

Just yesterday, Microsoft began rolling out an update for the Xbox PC app, making it faster and more responsive on Windows desktop and handheld. We've had a little play with the new version, and our first impressions are mostly positive.

Xbox boss Asha Sharma posted a short video showing off the boot speed of the revamped Xbox PC app. It took a mere 5.2 seconds to load into the home page, clocking in a full 10 seconds quicker than the current version.

Having tried the new Xbox PC app ourselves, we can confirm that it's noticeably faster than the current version. It opens wonderfully swift on my Windows 10 desktop, stocked with 64GB of Sam Altman's precious FU-RAM, but it's also pretty nippy on my first-gen ASUS ROG Ally.

It was important to me that this new version worked well on my ROG Ally, because the current one takes an age to boot in the handheld's 15W Windows mode. I've never enjoyed that feeling of being forced to switch the ROG Ally into Performance or Turbo mode just to get the Xbox PC app running. Now, I don't have to. Big W for this update!

Beyond the speed improvements, the new app looks so much cleaner and feels much more in line with the Xbox console experience, which has been something I've always hoped we'd see: a kinda merger between the PC and Xbox console interfaces, with the latter serving as more of a base.

The side bar is much slicker too. Social stuff like who's online and what they're up to now display alongside Home, Library, Game Pass, and Store options. Cloud Gaming has been removed from the left-hand bar though, which made it a little awkward to access.

I found launching a game via the cloud a bit confusing. Almost like it's been hidden on purpose. I expected to be able to head to a cloud-enabled title, open its game page, and find the button to launch it via the cloud. Just like before. However, there's nothing to select. It simply says "I own this". Instead, I had to head back to the library page, hit Select, open the submenu, and choose "Play on Cloud". It's handy, but took a little searching to get working.

Remote Play has also been tucked away in a dropdown menu for some reason. I'd much rather see it on the left, alongside the other main tab options. I reckon with a bit more time the new Xbox PC app will be fantastic, and with a couple of updates it should work out some of the kinks I mentioned above.

So far I think the app update is really slick, very fast, and a much nicer experience than the current version. It's a good step in the right direction, and that seems to be the general consensus among Xbox users online, too:

News Xbox PC App Receives Significant Upgrade Starting Today, Plus More Cloud Gaming Improvements

Sorry, but I never really know where to focus my attention. The navigation elements don't seem to be placed in logical locations, at least from my perspective, and the overall experience lacks consistency from one screen to another.

And Big Picture mode feels very old-school. It reminds me of an outdated Plex Media Server interface.

Honestly, I think Xbox is clearly moving in the right direction. It's still missing a few features, but overall it feels cleaner, more intuitive, and more user-friendly than Steam, which, in my opinion, has started to fall behind in terms of interface design and usability.

@RTGX Don't play the victim, that's a bit too easy.

You're entitled to your opinion, but statements like "it's light-years ahead" are hugely exaggerated and only highlight a lack of nuance and analysis.

For example, I'm not saying everything about Steam is bad. Quite the opposite. Some of the features available on Steam would be great additions to the Xbox app. But overall, and I want to stress that this is based on my personal preferences, I find the user experience and the overall design better thought out on Xbox.

That's my point of view, and clearly I'm not the only one in this comment thread who feels that way.

I just expect opinions to be a bit more balanced, and I'll admit I struggle with definitive, hyperbolic statements like the ones you're making. They tend to shut down any meaningful discussion rather than encourage it.

#4030. Here's What The Expanse: Osiris Reborn's Recast Main Character Looks and Sounds Like

Developer and publisher Owlcat Games has revealed the new face and voice of the male protagonist in The Expanse: Osiris Reborn.

Following negative feedback from fans, the company announced it would be recasting the role and making updates to the character's appearance.

In the below video, the revamped captain makes his debut:

The new voice is provided by actor Blythe Melin, who will perform as both the male protagonist and his brother, J.

The video also shows a quite dramatic visual change for the character's default look. Players will be able to fully customise their protagonist, but Owlcat says in a press release it's "important to have a default look players can use as a basis for their own captain."

"The developers have redesigned the male captain’s model to give him a less standard military personnel design with more detail and polish for players to work with. His handsome appearance is also matched by his new voice, brought to life by voice actor Blythe Melin, who previously worked on titles like Genshin Impact, Honkai Star Rail, Diablo IV, Ready or Not, and more. Blythe doesn’t just take over as the captain, he also voices his more carefree and relaxed identical twin J."

Owlcat adds that more information about additional members of the cast will be shared "at a later date."

As mentioned, the original version of the male captain was widely panned, a criticism we made in our hands-on preview earlier this year.

Early responses to the changes appear to be pretty positive, though, which is good news.

#4029. Iman Vellani wants everyone to know why X-Men: The Last Stand "failed"

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.
